characterization_methods.key_findings: Light gray OM micrograph with scattered small dark dots; dense small-grain boundary network; grain boundaries largely non-closed; images stitched from multiple smaller ones with visible horizontal/vertical stitching artifacts due to brightness variations
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: real size 604.98 × 403.90 µm; original resolution 5530 × 3692 pixels (figure_001); evaluation input resolution 1771 × 1061 pixels, 38 images (Table 1)
characterization_methods.purpose: Imaging polycrystalline single-phase HEA grain boundaries for microstructure segmentation evaluation

characterization_methods.key_findings: ARI: MatSAM 0.59 (±10.8%), SAM 0.56 (±6.0%), Canny 0.35 (±14.3%), OTSU 0.37 (±13.3%), Watershed 0.29 (±10.8%); F1: MatSAM 0.35 (±11.1%), SAM 0.52 (±11.5%), Canny 0.42 (±13.3%), OTSU 0.41 (±11.9%), Watershed 0.39 (±10.4%); Recall: MatSAM 0.24 (±7.8%), SAM 0.43 (±9.3%), Canny 0.33 (±10.4%), OTSU 0.34 (±9.4%), Watershed 0.33 (±8.7%). MatSAM achieves the best ARI (0.59) on HEA, higher than SAM (0.56) and the best rule-based method OTSU (0.37).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 38 test images; metrics ARI, F1, Recall reported as mean ± relative deviation (%)
characterization_methods.purpose: Quantitative evaluation of grain-boundary segmentation accuracy on the HEA dataset
characterization_methods.technique: MatSAM (training-free SAM-based) segmentation compared with SAM, Canny, OTSU and Watershed

defect_interactions.interaction_type: non-closed grain boundaries and protruding cracks
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Extensive non-closed grain boundaries and protruding cracks make segmentation particularly challenging

interfaces.interface_notes: Grain boundaries are the target objects of the boundary-type HEA dataset; the boundary network is dense; boundaries are largely non-closed, with stitching artifacts and cracks (single-phase, so no phase-phase interfaces)

defects.type: scattered dark dots (likely pores or second-phase particles)

phases_present.morphology: large equiaxed grains; coarse grains with faint, locally discontinuous/invisible boundaries

structures.overall_structure: Polycrystalline single-phase microstructure with large equiaxed grains

unmapped_findings: HEA is one of 11 microscopy datasets, grouped as 'boundary' type in Table 1 with evaluation metric Recall and 38 test images.
figure_001 identifies the HEA material as FeCoCrNiMn high-entropy alloy, whereas the in-text dataset description (b0024) and Table 1 (b0036) refer to it generically as 'high-entropy alloy'.
Dataset resolution is reported inconsistently: figure_001 gives 5530 × 3692 pixels (real size 604.98 × 403.90 µm), while Table 1 lists the evaluation input resolution as 1771 × 1061 pixels.
In figure_007(b) and b0082, some HEA grain boundaries are nearly invisible (non-closing, attributed to uneven or incomplete etching), yet MatSAM can infer the missing boundary parts.

b0062 notes that HEA micrographs exhibit grayscale values that vary little between adjacent grains but largely across regions, and figure_004 shows Canny is fragmented/noisy and Watershed leaves part of the field unsegmented while MatSAM matches the expert label.
